exceptions.title: Loopback and local origins may be potentially trustworthy
exceptions.condition: The origin matches a local or loopback case recognized by the potentially trustworthy origin algorithm.
exceptions.effect: The origin can satisfy the trustworthiness precondition without public HTTPS transport.
exceptions.security_consequence: Local development remains usable, but local service exposure and DNS or proxy assumptions still require review.
limitations: Potentially trustworthy does not prove that an application listening on loopback is correctly authenticated or isolated.

exceptions.title: User agents may designate development origins trustworthy
exceptions.condition: A user agent provides an explicit configuration for staging or development origins.
exceptions.effect: Configured origins may be treated as trustworthy even when the normal algorithm would return not trustworthy.
exceptions.security_consequence: A broad or hidden override can defeat a transport gate; review scope, user control, and deployment separation.
limitations: The specification does not standardize the configuration UX or enterprise policy surface.

exceptions.title: Authenticated packaged-application schemes may be trusted
exceptions.condition: A user agent authenticates the contents of a packaged-application URL scheme.
exceptions.effect: The user agent may treat the scheme as secure despite it not being HTTPS.
exceptions.security_consequence: Trust moves to package authenticity, update, and scheme-handler guarantees.
limitations: The source gives examples, not a cross-user-agent interoperable scheme registry.

exceptions.title: A powerful feature may override Permissions defaults
exceptions.condition: The feature's specification determines that the Permissions default types or algorithms are unsuitable.
exceptions.effect: The feature may define custom descriptors, state constraints, keying, result types, revocation, or a default state.
exceptions.security_consequence: Every override becomes a feature-specific security decision and must preserve user intent and composition with secure contexts and policy.
limitations: The ability to override is not evidence that any particular weaker default is safe.

exceptions.title: Permissions Policy can default a feature to every origin
exceptions.condition: A policy-controlled feature defines `*` as its default allowlist.
exceptions.effect: The feature is enabled in top-level and child documents unless a header or container policy narrows it.
exceptions.security_consequence: Cross-origin delegation becomes ambient, so sensitive features need a strong compatibility and threat-model justification.
limitations: The framework permits `*`; it does not classify which features can safely use it.

exceptions.title: Parent policy can explicitly delegate a feature
exceptions.condition: The inherited policy permits the feature and a header or container `allow` policy includes the child origin.
exceptions.effect: A child document can use the feature subject to its own permission and feature-specific checks.
exceptions.security_consequence: Delegation should be origin-specific and no broader than the embedded component's function.
limitations: Delegation does not grant a user permission by itself and cannot widen a parent-level denial.

exceptions.title: CSP unsafe sources explicitly re-enable risky behavior
exceptions.condition: A policy contains an unsafe source expression such as `unsafe-inline`, `unsafe-eval`, or a related narrowly specified keyword.
exceptions.effect: The corresponding inline or string-compilation restriction is relaxed as defined by the directive algorithms.
exceptions.security_consequence: The policy may lose core injection mitigation; use requires a documented compatibility need and narrower alternatives assessment.
limitations: Different directives interpret source expressions through directive-specific checks.

exceptions.title: strict-dynamic delegates trust from a nonce or hash
exceptions.condition: A script source list includes `strict-dynamic` and a root script is authorized by a nonce or hash.
exceptions.effect: Trust propagates to scripts loaded by that root according to CSP's script checks, while some host allowlist behavior changes.
exceptions.security_consequence: The root script and its loaders become a capability delegation boundary; script gadgets can expand effective authority.
limitations: This is deliberate delegation, not a general permission to treat all dynamically created code as safe.

exceptions.title: Trusted Types default policy can convert legacy strings
exceptions.condition: A realm defines a default Trusted Type policy and enforcement encounters a string for a protected sink.
exceptions.effect: The default policy receives an opportunity to produce the required Trusted Type; rejection still fails the sink operation.
exceptions.security_consequence: A permissive default policy can centralize but also conceal unsafe conversion, so validation and failure must be reviewed.

evidence.section: 3.5 Process value with a default policy

limitations: Policy code is application code and is not proved safe by the platform.

exceptions.title: Report-only policy observes without blocking
exceptions.condition: A policy is delivered through a report-only channel defined by CSP, Permissions Policy, Integrity Policy, Trusted Types integration, or Document Policy.
exceptions.effect: Violations are reported but the report-only policy does not authorize blocking behavior.
exceptions.security_consequence: Report-only is suitable for migration and telemetry but must not be counted as an enforced mitigation.
limitations: Each policy family defines its own report format, privacy risks, and coverage.

exceptions.title: Upgrade behavior is conditional and has no insecure fallback guarantee
exceptions.condition: A request is in an upgradeable category or the client has an upgrade-insecure-requests policy; otherwise mixed-content blocking rules apply.
exceptions.effect: Eligible URLs are rewritten to secure schemes; a failed secure fetch is not an authorization to retry insecurely.
exceptions.security_consequence: Compatibility failures are preferable to silent downgrade, but failure channels and navigation distinctions remain reviewable.
limitations: Exact categories and navigation handling depend on current Fetch and HTML integration.

exceptions.title: Cross-origin SRI requires an eligible response
exceptions.condition: Integrity verification is requested for a cross-origin resource.
exceptions.effect: The response must satisfy the fetch and CORS eligibility conditions required for integrity verification; otherwise the resource cannot be treated as a successful integrity match.
exceptions.security_consequence: This avoids turning integrity checks into cross-origin data oracles but requires server deployment support.
limitations: The precise fetch mode and destination integration must be checked in the consuming specification.

exceptions.title: Fetch Metadata may be absent or require compatibility handling
exceptions.condition: A request comes from a client or context that does not send the expected Sec-Fetch headers, including some non-browser, extension, or legacy traffic.
exceptions.effect: The server cannot apply a header-only isolation rule without an explicit fallback path.
exceptions.security_consequence: Fail-open preserves compatibility but weakens isolation; fail-closed needs a deployment inventory and staged rollout.
limitations: Compatibility populations and implementation support are deployment evidence, not specified by the header standard.

exceptions.title: Authors can select a more permissive referrer policy
exceptions.condition: A response, element, or request context supplies a policy such as `unsafe-url` or another value that discloses more information.
exceptions.effect: The referrer algorithm sends the policy-permitted origin or URL information.
exceptions.security_consequence: Capability tokens, path identifiers, or query data can leak to other origins; permissive policy needs an explicit data-flow justification.
limitations: The W3C snapshot's default differs from current living-standard behavior; this exception records selectable policies, not the current default.

exceptions.title: WebCrypto keeps getRandomValues outside the secure-context gate
exceptions.condition: Code calls `crypto.getRandomValues`; unlike `crypto.subtle`, `randomUUID`, and CryptoKey, this member lacks [SecureContext] in the cited IDL.
exceptions.effect: Cryptographically strong random values remain available in non-secure contexts.
exceptions.security_consequence: Do not generalize WebCrypto's secure-context gating from `subtle` to the entire `Crypto` interface.
limitations: Availability of randomness does not make the surrounding non-secure context trustworthy.

exceptions.title: Clear-Site-Data wildcard is intentionally forward-compatible
exceptions.condition: A response uses the `*` clearing type.
exceptions.effect: All current and future clearing types recognized by the user agent are requested, not only the types known when the header was authored.
exceptions.security_consequence: The wildcard is appropriate for broad cleanup but can cause future destructive scope expansion if used as shorthand.
limitations: The 2017 draft's clearing-type inventory can differ from later implementations or integrations.

exceptions.title: Credential mediation can be silent when explicitly permitted
exceptions.condition: The request uses a mediation mode and stored state for which Credential Management allows credential return without an interactive chooser.
exceptions.effect: A credential may be returned without fresh user interaction until preventSilentAccess or another state change requires mediation.
exceptions.security_consequence: Silent access must remain origin-bound and visible enough to avoid sign-in tracking or origin confusion.
limitations: Credential-type specifications can refine mediation semantics.

exceptions.title: Cross-origin DBSC single sign-on is a separate tentative deliverable
exceptions.condition: A design needs DBSC behavior across origins for single sign-on.
exceptions.effect: The base DBSC control is insufficient evidence; the charter lists a separate WICG incubation proposal.
exceptions.security_consequence: Do not infer cross-origin authority or scope expansion from the base DBSC specification.

evidence.section: Tentative deliverable: DBSC for Single Sign-On

limitations: The tentative deliverable is not mined in the initial mechanism catalog.

exceptions.title: Change-password discovery uses constrained temporary redirects
exceptions.condition: The well-known change-password resource directs the client to the actual account UI.
exceptions.effect: Servers should use 302, 303, or 307 and clients must handle those redirects; an HTML refresh fallback is also described.
exceptions.security_consequence: Redirect targets become security-sensitive and need origin, navigation, and UI review even though discovery starts at a trustworthy origin.

evidence.source_title: A Well-Known URL for Changing Passwords

limitations: The specification allows an HTML refresh fallback and requires clients to handle OK responses, so redirect-only assumptions are unsafe.

exceptions.title: Passkey endpoint discovery may return an empty object but never redirect
exceptions.condition: An RP wants to signal passkey support without advertising enroll, manage, or PRF-information URLs.
exceptions.effect: A 200 application/json response containing `{}` is allowed; a redirect remains forbidden.
exceptions.security_consequence: Clients must distinguish supported-without-links from malformed, redirected, or untrusted discovery responses.

evidence.source_title: A Well-Known URL for Relying Party Passkey Endpoints

limitations: The empty object signals support only; it does not expose a management capability.
